A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SynQuE and LENS study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream performance, proxy correlations, dataset-selection results and ablations across sentiment analysis, Text2SQL, image classification and web navigation.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds experiments on scorer backbones, component choices, sample sensitivity and hybrid scoring.

M1.justification: The core LENS rubric compilation and four-permutation debiasing procedure remain unchanged. Appendix B.8 adds an experimental scoring variant, alpha times LENS plus (1-alpha) times MDM, without replacing the original method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same financial sentiment data, three BIRD databases, three ImageNet class splits and WebVoyager/NNetNav coverage. The added appendix experiments vary configurations and sample counts within these existing tasks.

E2.justification: The main proxy and PERPLEXITY comparator sets are retained. v3 adds a comparison of logistic-regression, random-forest and two-layer-MLP implementations of PAD in Table 14, and compares hybrid scores with standalone LENS and MDM endpoints in Figure 3.

E3.justification: New appendix experiments vary scorer backbones, encoder and classifier choices, MDM cluster counts of 3/5/10/20, sentiment sample counts of 100/200 and hybrid weights. These are configuration extensions within the retained evaluation framework; the original task-training settings, splits and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B substantially expands the robustness investigation: scorer-family dependence, clustering sensitivity, alternative embeddings, PAD classifier dependence, LENS–MDM synergy and sentiment sample efficiency. The earlier preferential-bias, rubric-design and kernel ablations are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions average correlations over five seeds for sampling real inputs and report the same standard-deviation table, renumbered from Table 11 to Table 16. No additional uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial component, backbone and sensitivity results. Table 8 newly reports GPT-4.1 sentiment Spearman correlation of .28 before debiasing versus .07 after; Table 15 reports LENS Spearman correlations of -.13 and .38 with 100 and 200 real samples. Table 6 also reverses MDM correlation signs: the 25-sample average changes from -.47/-.54 to .47/.54 (Spearman/Pearson). Main Tables 2, 3 and 5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and Equations 1–8 remain unchanged. Appendix B.8 newly defines the hybrid quality function alpha times LENS plus (1-alpha) times MDM, a limited mathematical addition without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: formalizing annotation-free dataset ranking, benchmarking proxy metrics and introducing LENS for complex tasks. The abstract adds a code-release statement, but does not revise the central scientific claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix B.2 qualifies debiasing substantially: it can degrade stronger sentiment scorers, possibly by overriding useful intrinsic priors. B.6–B.9 add interpretations of encoder robustness, classifier dependence, absent hybrid synergy and task-dependent sample efficiency. These qualifications coexist with the unchanged, broader debiasing claims in Section 5.2.

D1.justification: v3 adds an author-code release statement and repository link, a BGE-M3 access reference, and identities/settings for the new ablations. Existing preprocessing instructions, prompts, serving configuration, hardware and hyperparameter disclosures are retained. Repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion and citations to Zhang et al. (2024), Hu et al. (2025) and Kuo et al. (2025). It more explicitly distinguishes SynQuE's dataset-level, label-free ranking from instance-level selection and weighting approaches requiring gradients or labeled validation data.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the prompt listings remain unchanged. Related work gains more specific subsections and revised positioning, while the appendix gains explanatory paragraphs and additional subsection organization.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is fully redrawn to expose the representation-based and LENS pipelines. v3 adds the hybrid plot, consolidates old and new backbone results in Table 8, and adds Tables 12–15. The appendix is substantially repacked, combining previously sparse pages and allowing prompt listings to span pages.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the expanded appendix better establishes sensitivity and failure conditions, particularly when debiasing hurts and when LENS needs more real samples. The code link also improves reproducibility information. These provide a limited net quality gain, weakened by Section 5.2 retaining blanket debiasing claims despite Table 8's counterexamples and by the redrawn Figure 1 ambiguously labeling task-model training 'No Labels Used'.
